title: Steering the AI
caption: markdown-harness steers the machine half
prose: A document can tell you how much of itself to believe. Not full trust — a floor that holds, and a reliable signal when a human needs to act.

raising-the-floor.description: A document can declare how much of itself to believe; reliable signals warn when humans must step in.

tool-boundary.description: markdown-harness steers the machine layer and prepares signals without claiming human judgment.

raising-the-floor.title: Steering the AI
raising-the-floor.keywords: markdown-harness, raise floor, steer arrow, human boundary
raising-the-floor.script: So the goal is to make the machine's half do more. And this is what I've been building over the past couple of weeks: markdown-harness. The idea is one sentence: a document can tell you how much of itself to believe. It's not about generating trust. Trust is semantic — a machine can never produce it. What it can do is raise the floor. Reliable signals that tell an agent or a human that something needs attention. You've seen these three circles before: deterministic, cheap, fast signals handed to the AI while it's working. The machine column reaching into the AI column. That's the arrow. And the human side is greyed out on purpose: this tool stops before it. That part was always yours.
